title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This is not a handwritten note on PD de Rham complexes. It is a typed page, numbered '- 58 -' of Exposé IX, from Grothendieck's 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie' (SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, §5.3), filed in this cote. The setting is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field K and residue characteristic p. A is an abelian variety over K and A' is its dual, with Néron models whose identity components are A° and A'°. The special fibres A_0° and A'_0° are extensions of abelian varieties B_0 and B'_0 by affine groups (a torus part and a unipotent part). The Tate modules T_ℓ(A°) are taken over S: for ℓ = p they are understood via p-divisible / finite flat group schemes. Each has a 'fixed part' with a toric part inside it, and the 'abelian part' (exponent ab) is the quotient of the fixed part by the toric part. The orthogonality theorem gives a pairing (5.3.2) between these abelian parts. On this page it is induced by (5.3.3), T_ℓ(A°)^ab × T_ℓ(A'°)^ab → T_ℓ(G_{m,S}), obtained by passing to quotients from the Weil-type pairing (5.2.4.2) coming from the canonical biextension. That pairing is perfect on the generic fibres, i.e. the map (5.3.4) T_ℓ(A°)^ab → D(T_ℓ(A'°)^ab) to the Cartier/Pontryagin dual is an isomorphism generically. One wants it to be an isomorphism over all of S, equivalently on the special fibre. For ℓ ≠ p this is trivial, since the objects are étale (locally constant) over S. For ℓ = p in mixed characteristic it follows from Tate's full faithfulness theorem for p-divisible groups over a complete DVR of characteristic 0 (Tate, 'p-divisible groups', th. 4). Grothendieck announces a direct proof avoiding Tate (7.4.6). He then interprets the statement geometrically: on the special fibre, (5.3.3) becomes the pairing (5.3.5) T_ℓ(B_0) × T_ℓ(B'_0) → T_ℓ(G_{m,k}), induced by the biextension W_0 of (A_0°, A'_0°) by G_m after passing to the quotients B_0, B'_0. Perfectness amounts to W_0 inducing a duality between the abelian parts B_0 and B'_0 of the reductions. This page states the key step of Grothendieck's orthogonality theorem / duality of the abelian parts of Néron model reductions.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. The claim that the ℓ ≠ p case is 'trivial' is standard: a morphism of étale sheaves over a henselian DVR that is an isomorphism generically, between objects that are locally constant over S, is an isomorphism.

Archival note: this typed SGA 7 IX page appears misfiled among the handwritten notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. It has no mathematical connection to the neighbouring pages, which compute PD algebras S{U_0,...,U_{n-1}}[dU_i].

ideas.what: Pairing between the abelian parts of the Tate modules (or p-divisible groups) of the Néron models of A and its dual, induced by the canonical biextension; it is perfect over all of S, and on the special fibre this means B_0 and B'_0 are dual via W_0.
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's orthogonality theorem / duality of abelian parts of Néron model reductions

ideas.what: Use of Tate's theorem on full faithfulness of p-divisible groups over mixed-characteristic DVRs to extend a generic isomorphism to an isomorphism over S, and its avoidance by a direct argument.
ideas.modern_name: Tate's full faithfulness theorem for p-divisible groups
ideas.where_published: Cited as [33, th.4] in SGA 7 IX

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX (§5.3), so its content is fully in the literature and credited to Grothendieck. The only curiosity is archival: it is filed within the 1976 PD de Rham notes.
transcription_corrections: The page is typed, not handwritten: it is p. 58 of Exposé IX of SGA 7 ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'). The archive numbers 376 and 198 are written at the bottom and in the margin.
In (5.3.5) and the following line, B'_o, A_o^o and A'_o^o carry subscript o (special fibre) and superscript o (identity component). The transcription is essentially correct.
'(5.3.4)' has a bold opening parenthesis in the image; the transcription is otherwise accurate.
